thread:
anna: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a "grace period" cutover for CP peering -> private endpoint for a subset of customers. Goal: zero customer traffic loss and clear rollback path. Thoughts?

mike: +1 to having a backstop. Curious how you imagine the grace window working in practice. A few options: dual-accept (both peering and endpoint), or a proxy fallback that rewrites to old path.

anna: My sketch: during cutover window we accept both connectors for the tenant. Control plane will prefer private endpoint but falling back to peered relay if health/probes fail. We log a mismatch metric and trigger alert if >1% of requests hit the fallback for >10m.

raj: Concern: dual-accept means we need consistent session affinity and src-ip preservation. If a customer relies on preserved srcip for their egress ACLs, switching path could break them. Do we have a reliable way to preserve src-ip across both modes?

sofia: For src-ip preservation we can do two things: 1) maintain ephemeral NAT mapping on relay side so the outbound IP matches expected pool, or 2) advertise a per-tenant egress IP via ENI/Elastic IP when private endpoint is active. Both have ops costs.

mike: Ops cost note — ENI approach scales badly on high-tenant count. Ephemeral NAT mapping is cheaper but adds complexity for connection tracking and health-based cleanup. Also RPF on customer's side could drop traffic if src-ip changes mid-session.

anna: Right. That's why the grace period should also include a preflight: short-lived probe that checks for ACL acceptance at customer egress. Idea: before shifting a tenant, run a probe that: 
```bash
curl -sS https://tenant-egress-check.example/verify -H "X-Secret: $TOKEN"
```
If that fails we skip the tenant and surface to SE.

raj: What about token TTLs and bootstrapping? If we accept both connectors simultaneously we need the controlplane to reconcile ephemeral bootstrap tokens so agents don't rotate away mid-window. We should set bootstrap token TTL = window + buffer and only rotate after auto-cutover completes.

sofia: Agree. Also require a 'grace-accept' flag in the connector handshake: the agent advertises accepted-peers=[peering,private] and CP marks which is primary. That simplifies reconciliation and operator visibility.

mike: Implementation detail: when agent claims dual acceptance, CP should expose metrics: primary_choice, fallback_count, last_fail_reason. We can wire to console dashboards and a single SLA-rollback playbook that can flip primary back to peering per-tenant.

anna: Rollback path: if fallback_count > threshold OR healthcheck fails for > X minutes we auto-roll back that tenant to peering-only and notify on-call + the tenant owner. Manual override still possible via console.

raj: One more risk: route flaps during BGP peering changes if customer uses dynamic routing. For customers with BGP, we should avoid simultaneous announcement changes. Instead, do a staged route withdraw: withdraw on CP region A, wait for global convergence window, then withdraw on region B. Document windows per-provider.

sofia: Also add a 'staged cutover' API that accepts parameters: { tenants: [...], window: "2026-04-07T02:00Z/04:00Z", strategy: "dual-accept|proxy-fallback|staged-bgp" } so SEs can coordinate.

mike: Thumbs up. Observability checklist: route-change diffs, probe success history, per-tenant fallback ratio, NAT mapping churn, and a synthetic user-journey sampling to detect app-level regressions.

anna: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with the concrete API, token TTL defaults, metrics, and the rollback thresholds. Action items:
- anna: RFC draft + proposed defaults
- mike: dashboard mockups for fallback_count & probe history
- raj: BGP staged withdraw steps and vendor-specific windows
- sofia: connector handshake flag + token TTL recommendation

ops-bot: Scheduled reminder set for 2026-04-05 15:00 to review RFC draft. :bell:

sofia: Minor nit — add a safety TTL for the grace mode on agents so a stray tenant doesn't stay in dual-accept forever if CP loses orchestration. Agents should revert after TTL unless renewed.

anna: Good call. I'll include agent-side TTL and a renewal heartbeat in the RFC. Thanks all, I'll post the draft in this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:
